Na! Natoota…|Oola refuses Jabba's advances|[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (paperback novel)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]]}} '''Oola''' was a [[Color|green]]-skinned [[Twi'lek]] [[Gender|female]] from a [[Oola's clan|clan]] on the [[planet]] [[Ryloth]]. She was kidnapped by [[Bib Fortuna]]—[[majordomo]] of the [[crime lord]] Jabba Desilijic Tiure—who had her taught exotic dancing and told her many lies about the grandeur of [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]. She was offered a chance to escape enslavement while in the [[city]] of [[Mos Eisley]], but chose to take her chances at the palace based on the lies she had heard. Fortuna then presented Oola as a gift to Jabba, who took a special interest in her and often had her dance with another enslaved dancer, [[Yarna d'al' Gargan]]. During Oola's [[time]] at the palace, she witnessed Jabba host various guests, including the [[bartender]] [[Shrem]], whom he fed to his pet [[rancor]], [[Pateesa]], and the [[bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett]], who delivered the [[smuggler]] [[Han Solo]] to the crime lord. In [[4 ABY]], Oola was sat with Jabba on his [[throne]] when the [[droid]]s [[R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO]] delivered a message from their master, [[Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker]], asking to bargain for Solo's freedom. She later danced with Gargan for the Hutt and his court during a performance of the [[Music|song]] "[[Jedi Rocks]]" by the [[Max Rebo Band]]; however, during the performance Jabba tried to pull her closer and she resisted. As punishment for embarrassing him, Jabba dropped Oola through a trap door into the rancor pit, where the dancer was devoured by Pateesa while the crime lord's court cheered. ==Biography== ===Kidnapping and enslavement=== [[File:Geezum-Oola-ROTJ.png|thumb|left|250px|Other beings watched as Oola danced.]] A [[Twi'lek]] [[Gender|female]] Oola was [[Reproduction|born]] to the [[Oola's parent|chieftain]]{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=Oola - Twi'lek Dancer}} of a primitive [[Oola's clan|clan]] on her [[species]]' [[homeworld]] of [[Ryloth]] and had a [[Oola's sister|sister]] and two nieces. She devoted herself to sensual dancing, and was trained at a celebrated school, but was betrayed by a jealous rival, after which she continued to encounter setbacks.''[[Return of the Jedi: Beware the Power of the Dark Side!]]'' The Twi'lek [[Bib Fortuna]], [[majordomo]] of the [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] then kidnapped Oola from the clan leading her to become [[Slavery|enslaved]]. He then had other Twi'leks train Oola in the art of exotic dancing so that he could present her to his employer as a present.''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]'' Fortuna transported Oola to the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]] and lied to her about the supposed glories awaiting her at [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]]. Before he delivered her there, a stranger in the [[city]] of [[Mos Eisley]] offered her a chance to escape. Although accepting that or other offers would have been opportunities to avoid life in the palace, Oola believed Fortuna; she preferred to take her chances and wished to see the Hutt's home for herself. Fortuna then delivered her to the palace and to Jabba. ===Dancing for her life=== [[File:Max_Rebo_Band_applause.png|thumb|right|260px|Oola (left) and Yarna d'al' Gargan (right) were a contrasting pair when they danced duets.]] At the palace, Oola was forced to wear an uncomfortable, flimsy [[Clothing|outfit]] made of black netting. It included a [[belt]] made from [[leather]] straps, a black and gray headpiece, black sandals, and a gray collar with a chain attached. Jabba paid considerable attention to Oola as he found her highly desirable, but she refused to give into him''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' and denied his advances, leaving her with no other choice''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' but to dance for her life while chained to his throne. She would regularly dance duets with the [[Askajian]] [[Yarna d'al' Gargan]], another enslaved dancer. Oola's dainty, graceful choreography contrasted with Gargan's slower, more deliberate moves,{{Databank|yarna-d-al-gargan|Yarna d'al' Gargan}} which were often humorously improvised. In [[3 ABY]],{{Aphra2016Date|annual3}} she was among those in Jabba's [[throne]] room when the [[bartender]] [[Shrem]] presented the Hutt with a [[spitscuttle]], which spat in the crime lord's face, leading to Shrem being dropped alongside the [[Trandoshan]] [[Skikkesk]] through a trap door into the pit below the room where Jabba kept his pet [[rancor]],[[Doctor Aphra Annual 3|''Doctor Aphra Annual'' 3]] [[Pateesa]].''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]'' She was later present in the throne room again when the [[bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett]] delivered the [[smuggler]] [[Han Solo]] to Jabba after Solo had been frozen in [[carbonite]].[[War of the Bounty Hunters 5|''War of the Bounty Hunters'' 5]] At some point after Solo's arrival in the palace, Oola followed fellow palace performer [[Jess]] in examining Solo's carbonite slab while Jabba and his retinue were away on the [[Khetanna]]. Jess noticed that Oola was notably in high spirits at the time, something that had become more of a rarity due to the nature of her circumstances. Oola noted the handsome features on Solo's face would be evident if not for his screams at the time of his freezing, with Jess agreeing. Oola then noted her incredulity at the thought that Solo had been caught by Jabba at last. Jess offered the idea that smugglers simply let their guard down eventually, but Oola countered with her own idea that Jabba simply caught everyone in the end. Upon hearing footsteps approaching, Oola and Jess became frightened, fearing for what would happen if they were caught. They soon saw that the new arrival was [[Damaris Viell]], another palace performer who then advised them to hunker down before Jabba caught them sniffing around, as his barge was due to arrive in fifteen minutes.{{StoryCite|story=Dune Sea Songs of Salt and Moonlight|book=From a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi}} Early one morning in [[4 ABY]], Oola was perched on the edge of Jabba's throne with the Hutt when the [[droid]]s [[R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO]] were brought before the crime lord with a message from their master, the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker]]. Oola and Jabba watched the [[Hologram|holographic]] message, in which Skywalker asked to bargain with Jabba for the freedom of the Jedi's friend Solo and gifted the Hutt the two droids as a sign of good will. When the message ended, Jabba merely laughed and declared he would not be giving up his favorite decoration, as he displayed the frozen smuggler on the wall of the throne room. ===The last dance=== {{Quote|Aah!''"
"''Whoops! Uh-oh!''"
"''Aah!|Oola screams as Sy Snootles reacts to her being dropped into the rancor pit|}} Shortly before [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] and the [[Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca]] arrived as part of the plan to [[Rescue of Han Solo|rescue]] Solo, the [[Max Rebo Band]] performed for Jabba and his court. Oola and Gargan gracefully danced together to the song in front of Jabba's throne, and when it ended the Hutt demanded Oola repeat her performance. Misinterpreting this as an order directed at them, the band began playing an improvised version of the [[Music|song]] "[[Jedi Rocks]]."{{SW|url=news/music-in-the-star-wars-galaxy-the-modal-nodes-vs-the-max-rebo-band|text=Music in the ''Star Wars'' Galaxy: The Modal Nodes vs. The Max Rebo Band|int=Music in the Star Wars Galaxy: The Modal Nodes vs. The Max Rebo Band}} Oola and Gargan once again began to dance, but, wanting to bring the Twi'lek closer, the Hutt brutally yanked the chain attached to Oola's collar. [[File:OolaRancorPit-ROTJ.png|thumb|left|250px|Oola lands in the pit of Pateesa]] Oola openly resisted the Hutt's advances, and for this public humiliation, Jabba dropped the dancer through the trap door into the pit below the throne room. The sudden interruption to the music elicited shock from other performers including the singers [[Sy Snootles]], [[Joh Yowza]], [[Rystáll Sant]], [[Lyn Me]], and [[Greeata Jendowanian]]. Oola rolled upon hitting the floor of the pit and then threw her chain behind her and stared up through a grating at the throne room where court members excitedly began to cheer and gathered to watch her fate. The Twi'lek's attention was then drawn to a large door into the pit that began to open, revealing Pateesa behind it. As Gargan watched helplessly while laughing, Oola screamed in fear before being eaten alive by the beast. Many of those who had cheered on Oola's demise, including Jabba himself, would perish themselves just the next day during Skywalker, Organa and Chewbacca's rescue of Solo. ===Legacy=== {{Quote|But they are part of the story… From what I gathered from Jess, Oola was a Twi'lek. She had been tricked into coming there. And her very last moment, her very last dance, was one of defiance. She pulled away from Jabba, and he punished her by feeding her to his rancor. I want to make sure that they have as much space in our record as someone like me does. Because Oola will never get to love—or grow old, or decide if she is going to be a wife next…|Leia Organa, on Oola|}} [[File:Oola-RotJAVA.png|thumb|250px|right|Oola's legacy lived on through the chronicle of Dora Mar and in the hearts of her loved ones.]] Despite her death at the hands of the rancor, Oola's legacy still lived on through the memories of her fellow dancers. When Luke killed the rancor, Lyn Me believed he had done so did to avenge Oola. Greeata expressed her skepticism, to which Me implored the [[Rodian]] to let her fantasize. Max Rebo would also reflect on how Oola left behind a sister and two nieces, all of whom had cared for her. When Leia Organa was captured during her attempt to rescue Solo, Jabba forced her to replace Oola as his favorite slave dancer. While Jess was helping dress Organa in a [[dancing-girl costume]], she told her about Oola and her gruesome demise. Jabba's decision to enslave Organa turned out to be his downfall when the princess strangled him to death with the chain that he enslaved her with. As Organa was later briefed by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebellion]] chronicler [[Dora Mar]] about the rescue mission, Organa told her about Oola and Jess because she wanted them to be remembered. ==Personality and traits== [[File:OolaGargan-Dancing-ROTJ.png|thumb|left|300px|Oola dancing for the last time]] Oola had an [[Color|olive green]] complexion, a delicate neck, and black [[eye]]s. The Twi'lek stood 1.6 [[meter]]s (5 [[foot]], 3 inches) tall. She was enthralled by the stories of grandeur that Fortuna told her about Jabba's Palace and turned down opportunities to escape so that she could see it. The Twi'lek danced with dainty and graceful choreography and was younger and slimmer than her regular dance partner Gargan.{{Databank|yarna-d-al-gargan|Yarna d'al' Gargan}} Jabba had a vile temper and would drastically punish those who did not please him, but even with this knowledge, Oola's revulsion toward the Hutt overcame her fear and she refused to give in to Jabba's advances. Despite her agility, she was unable to escape from the rancor. ==Equipment== While enslaved, Oola was forced to wear an uncomfortable, flimsy [[Clothing|outfit]] made of black netting. It included a [[belt]] made from [[leather]] straps, a black and gray headpiece, black sandals, and a gray collar with a chain attached. ==Behind the scenes== Oola was portrayed by [[Femi Taylor]] in the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film, {{Film|VI}}, in both the original release and in additional scenes filmed later for the [[1997]] [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]]. Since Taylor's appearance was almost unchanged after 14 years, she could film a close-up of Oola's terror at the rancor,{{InsiderCite|34|In the Star Wars Universe|In the ''Star Wars'' Universe: Femi Taylor}} extending the scene by a few seconds.''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' [[File:Oola-Maquette.png|thumb|right|300px|A prototype maquette of Oola]] Oola's cone-shaped hearing organs were made from [[Wikipedia:Foam rubber|foam rubber]] so that they would be malleable in a way similar to earlobes.{{SW|url=news/much-to-learn-you-still-have-7-things-you-might-not-know-about-twileks|text=Much to Learn You Still Have: 7 Things You Might Not Know About Twi'leks}} Her [[lekku]] were made with foam latex in order to be as light as possible so that they respond to Taylor's gestures or movements. They were blended into the actress's green skin makeup, which took four hours to apply.''[[Star Wars: Women of the Galaxy]]'' An early prototype maquette of Oola had blue skin, while later prototype maquettes depicted her with red skin and white hair.''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]'' According to Femi Taylor in a [[TheForce.net]] interview, during the early development of ''Return of the Jedi'', Oola was meant to have a major part in the scenes at Jabba's Palace because her fate was not to be eaten by Jabba's rancor. Instead, Oola was to survive and escape from Jabba's Palace. Although director [[Richard Marquand]] storyboarded the sequence of Oola's escape, it was cut because of budget constraints, so the character's role was considerably reduced, as well as her fate.{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/jedicouncil/interview/femitaylor.asp|text=TheForce.Net - Jedi Council - Interviews | Femi Taylor|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20171126075443}} In an interview with the ''Aggressive Negotiations'' podcast, ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' writer [[Henry Gilroy]] stated that the events of the [[Battle of Ryloth]] in that series likely involved many Twi'leks being sold into slavery by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], going on to suggest that Oola may have been brought to Jabba's Palace as a result.{{WebCite|url=https://www.spreaker.com/user/10684996/an-181#|text=Issue 181: Henry Gilroy: The Ryloth Arc|author=John Mills & Matthew Rushing|date=2019-09-20|format=Podcast|work=''Aggressive Negotiations: A Star Wars Pod''|archivedate=20200709073437}} ==Appearances== *{{StoryCite|story=Everyone's a Critic (short story)|book=From a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi|audiobook=1}} *''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]'' {{Imo}} *''[[Star Wars Treasury: The Original Trilogy]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Original Trilogy – A Graphic Novel]]'' *[[Doctor Aphra Annual 3|''Doctor Aphra Annual'' 3]] *[[War of the Bounty Hunters 5|''War of the Bounty Hunters'' 5]] *{{StoryCite|story=Dune Sea Songs of Salt and Moonlight|book=From a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi|audiobook=1}} *{{Film|VI}} {{1st}} *[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (paperback novel)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]] *''[[Return of the Jedi: Beware the Power of the Dark Side!]]'' {{Ab|Return of the Jedi: Beware the Power of the Dark Side!
